item.title: Bridges & Brunch with Strasburg Scooter Tours — Fri Jul 24 — Strasburg Scooter Tours
item.description:
Experience a relaxing morning ride through the back roads of Amish Country in Lancaster County, PA. Along the way to a 19th century covered bridge, enjoy the scenery of rolling hills, breathtaking views, and our Amish neighbors going about their daily routines. Itinerary Duration: 1.5-2 hours Some of our past tours have included:
A guided tour of one of Lancaster County’s most beautiful covered bridges An opportunity for a close up of daily life in Amish Country $10 dining voucher to one of two of Strasburg’s favorites brunch spots, Casey Jones’ Restaurant and Speckled Hen*
And each trip is unique, so you never know what we might have in store for you! *Unfortunately, we regret to inform you that some of the food offerings on the tour may not be considered ‘Kosher.’ We apologize for any inconvenience.
Source: Discover Lancaster

item.title: Lancaster Breakfast and History Walking Tour — Fri Jul 24, 9:00 AM — Unique Lancaster
item.description:
Searching for a walking history tour in Lancaster? You’re in for a flavorful experience—literally!
Introducing the Lancaster History & Breakfast Walking Tour—a dynamic two-hour adventure that blends the rich heritage of one of America’s oldest inland cities with a delicious morning meal. Explore Lancaster’s vibrant streets with a professionally trained local guide and journey through time from the early 1700s through the transformative decades of the 20th century.
Brought to you by Unique Lancaster Experiences, this guided walk kicks off with your choice of hot or iced coffee or tea to energize your morning. Along the way, you’ll hear engaging stories about Lancaster’s evolution as a bustling Market City and its transition from trolleys to automobiles after WWI.
But this isn’t your standard history tour. You’ll dive into interactive discussions and uncover captivating insights about colonial life, architectural landmarks, and the impact of prohibition on the region.

item.title: Tommy James & The Shondells at American Music Theatre — Fri Jul 24, 7:30 PM — American Music Theatre
item.description: Relive the soundtrack of a generation when Tommy James & The Shondells take the stage for a night of nonstop hits and pure nostalgia. With an incredible string of chart-topping classics, this legendary group helped define the sound of the late ’60s and early ’70s — and their music continues to ignite audiences around the world. Sing along to iconic favorites like “Crimson and Clover,” “Mony Mony,” “I Think We’re Alone Now,” “Hanky Panky,” and “Mirage.” Packed with unforgettable melodies, driving rhythms, and timeless pop-rock energy, this concert delivers hit after hit in a high-octane live performance that spans decades of musical history. Whether you grew up with these songs on the radio or discovered them through movies, commercials, and modern covers, Tommy James & The Shondells bring a feel-good evening of classic rock that’s perfect for fans of all ages. Don’t miss your chance to experience these legendary songs performed live — a night of memories, music, and pure fun awaits.

item.title: Children's Chapel — Sun Jul 26, 10:30 AM — Saint James Episcopal Church
item.description:
Children’s Chapel* meets weekly during the 10:30 AM Sunday Mass. Children and youth ages 3 and above begin the morning in the sanctuary where they can experience the processional and the opening congregational prayers. After the opening Collect, children are invited to the front of the sanctuary to make their way to the chapel and participate in songs, prayers, brief meditation and storytelling of the day’s Gospel and/or New and Old Testament readings. The Godly Play® teaching method includes using beautiful wooden figures, candles, and symbolic colors to aid our storytelling as we listen to God’s word for us. Children often respond to the story using simple art supplies including crayons, construction paper, origami paper and Model Magic air dry clay. Children return to the Sanctuary during the passing of the Peace. They are welcome to take part in Holy Communion.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Ride the Jack Markel/ Battery Park Trails 21 miles flat — Sun Jul 26, 2:00 PM
item.description:
Lancaster Bicycle Club (LBC) Meetup 15 folks have already signed up for this ride from the Wolverton Club. Join your bicycle riding friends from the LBC Club and Wilmington Rails Trails for one of our most popular rides, a trail ride on the Industrial-Jack Markell Trail from Wilmington to New Castle. In New Casket we will ride a couple miles up the Delaware Bay on Battery Park Trail. Turning back we will ride back to Wilmington where we will stop and eat along the Riverfront at Timothy’s Riverfront Grill. There is plenty of parking in the parking lot of the DuPont Environmental Center. This is a casual ride. Please do not go on this ride if you are not willing to stay with the group and wear a helmet. No one will be left behind. Like always helmets are required. Have a tube with you so someone can fix your flat. This trail is paved or wooden bridges, so any kind of bicycle will do. Richard Conner, Leader 717-572-8480
Source: Meetup: Lancaster Bicycle Club

item.title: Vespers — Sun Jul 26, 5:00 PM — Saint James Chapel
item.description:
Vespers, Sunday evenings at 5:00 PM | In person only A contemplative candlelit service to nurture mind, body and spirit Join us for Vespers, a warm and inviting weekly gathering in the serene surroundings of the Saint James Chapel. This quiet, reflective service embraces the rich prayer traditions of Christianity and the embodied practices that nurture our spiritual lives today. Engage in uplifting singing, find solace in moments of silence, and choose the posture that feels most comfortable for you as we open our hearts to listen for God’s voice. We have meditation cushions, yoga mats, and chairs available for your comfort. We’ll celebrate Holy Communion on the third Sunday of the month. We can’t wait to see you there! In person only. Everyone is welcome—come as you are! Over the summer, Vespers will be held on June 21, July 26 and August 23rd.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Valued Volunteers – Together We Read — Mon Jul 27, 1:00 PM — Burrowes Elementary
item.description:
The School District of Lancaster is inviting community members to become part of Valued Volunteers – Together We Read, a districtwide initiative that connects volunteers with students to help strengthen reading skills on Monday, July 27, at 1:00 pm – 3:00 pm at Burrowes Elementary School located at 101 Ranck Ave. Lancaster PA. The training serves as both the district’s required Valued Volunteers orientation and a kickoff for the Together We Read initiative. Participants will learn about the volunteer process while also receiving reading strategies, tips, and resources they can use when reading with students in our schools. No teaching experience is necessary. If you’re a first-time volunteer or returning to support SDoL students, the training will provide the tools and confidence needed to make every reading session meaningful.
Volunteers play an important role in helping students build literacy skills and a love of reading. By sharing your time, you can make a lasting difference

The short service of Compline is based on the closing time of prayer in the Daily Office, or monastic cycle of prayer. It is observed in monasteries around 8 or 9 PM when darkness has fallen and bedtime is near.
The thoughts that inspire the prayers during Compline are the need for divine forgiveness and protection against the powers of darkness. Prayers for peace and rest are offered as night falls.
People of all faiths and beliefs are invited to this contemplative service. The service lasts about 20 minutes.
Source: Saint James Lancaster

item.title: Monthly Club Meeting - “Sparrows Simplified: Making Sense of LBJ’s” — Thu Sep 10, 7:00 PM — North Museum of Nature and Science
item.description: Club Meeting – North Museum of Nature and Science, 400 College Ave, Lancaster, PA 17603 Presented by Michael Moore, retired Biology professor and past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society Many birders struggle with identifying sparrows, referring to them as LBJ’s (little brown jobs) or sparrow sp. This talk will help you tackle this difficult group. It will discuss and then attempt to blend the two main approaches to identification, the Peterson System and the Cape May School, to lead you to sparrow identification confidence. Each of the 16 species of regularly occurring sparrows in this area will be compared and contrasted with some discussion of finding and identifying rarities. Mike is a retired Biology Professor and a past president of the Delaware Ornithological Society. He started birding in middle school in Massachusetts and has had a life longpassion for birds. He completed his PhD at the University of Washington on the field endocrinology of White-crowned Sparr

item.description:

Bring chairs and a lunch. The site has public restrooms and a pavilion. Target species will include Broad-winged Hawk, American Kestrel, Osprey, Bald Eagle and Sharp-shinned Hawk.
